Anyhow, as stated above, thanks to the North brothers and the latest find from over the border, Joe Reilly, we won the team race for the first time.

Winner of the second 'race', for 5th place, was Tony Fairclough who just held off Trevor Hart and Joe Reilly. Finishing behind 20 years old Reilly was a runner exactly twice Joe's age - that elder statesman of the running fraternity, Jack Brown.

Joe Reilly was starting to make some impression after a slowish start and Howard Satchell, who was originally only reserve, had dispatched Chris Keavey etc. and for a few glorious miles had his sights trained on Ranjit Bhatia and John Dear.
Our sixth scorer was 20 years old Joe Reilly, who had only come in as reserve but rose to the occasion in great style--taking 30 places in the final lap and finishing a creditable 134th.

Only three runners were with him at half a mile (2:15/13:30 pace!) - Joe Reilly, Adrian Major and Alan Black. It was obvious that he could not maintain this sort of speed for long and as he tired Joe strode out in front.

Joe Reilly did the donkey work for the first 3 miles, with Alan Black then taking over. When North broke away Reilly, Fairclough and O'Hara chased hard, dropping Alan in the process, but Black recovered well and showing great determination ran through again only to fail by a mere inch to add a "silv…

The result augured well for the Johnstone Relay the following week at Hornchurch, for to supplement our heroes of Blackheath we had Gerry North, Joe Reilly, Laurie O'Hara, Mel Thorpe, Trevor Hart and Charlie Dabbs, with Fairclough and Black withdrawing.
'B' · J.Reilly · 14:39

Charlie Dabbs showed his strength on the hills once again by shaking off Joe Reilly to take 3rd place and, but for going off course along the Ridgway, Ranjit Bhatia would have finished 5th (a former record holder too!)

STAGE 10: Joe Reilly (16:06 - 2nd fastest) Joe was unable to maintain our sub-16 sequence but the latter stages of these longer races are notoriously slower, which may be of some consolation, but only serves to underline the speed of Valley's Mike Wiggs who broke John Thresher's 1½ hour old record with a time of 15:13!
We were, indeed, even sorrier to lose that other Scotsman Joe Reilly. Joe has turned in some excellent performances for Belgrave and his support for the club was always greatly appreciated.
Another missing from our Belgrave Relay dozen of last year is Joe Reilly, but with Geoff North standing down on that occasion we should be stronger this year, despite the loss of Mel and Joe.
Joe Reilly · Sep 66
